# CORE-TGT-02

**Is every departure from the target state recorded as a decision, and is a time-bound one given an expiry and a path back?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [Core architecture lens](core.md) 0.6.0 |
| Area | TGT: Target state |
| Default severity | major |
| Decided by | A tool checks presence; a reviewer judges |
| Reads | `decisions.departure` |

## Why it matters

TOGAF grants dispensations rather than ignoring departures, and G253 offers three answers to one: enforce the target, grant time-bound relief, or change the target.

## Rule

Every decision with departure set has status accepted, chosen, rationale and departure.from; a departure with kind time-bound also has expires and path_back. With no decision that has departure set, the tool half is not-applicable, not met, and the reviewer half decides. A reviewer checks that no departure has gone unrecorded, reading the target-state positions in the triage record.

## Sources

- The Open Group, TOGAF Standard 10th Edition, Enterprise Architecture Capability and Governance, chapter 6, Architecture Compliance (`togaf-compliance`)
